newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar seen further eroding kiwifruit returns.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar seen further eroding kiwifruit returns.

text.p: Currency fluctuations cost New Zealand kiwifruit growers NZ$53 million in sales over 1996/97 and could wipe out $60 million in the current year to March, Zespri International chief executive Robin Mills said on Tuesday.
Mills told Kiwifruit New Zealand's annual meeting in Tauranga that the New Zealand dollar's fluctuations over the current year would again be the single biggest detractor for grower returns.
Kiwifruit New Zealand, formerly the New Zealand Kiwifruit Marketing Board, split off its marketing role to Zespri International early this year.
Growers would be hit with a "double whammy" when the two main trading currencies, the mark and the yen, were converted back to New Zealand dollars, Mills said.

The New Zealand dollar had risen steadily against the mark since 1994 and at the end of the last season it was 16 percent higher than the previous year. The New Zealand dollar had also firmed 18 percent against the yen over the same year.
"The New Zealand dollar's rise has affected returns more detrimentally than any other season," he said.

"Managing the risks of exchange rate movements is a fact of life for any exporter. But, if we take last year's return of NZ$275 million and apply the June 4 spot rate, we're looking at almost NZ$60 million off returns," he said.
Forward cover would claw back some ground, but the consequences of a high dollar would still be felt by exporters.
Twenty-four weeks into the current season the crop was smaller in size and volume was less than ideal.
But Mills said 1997 had started promisingly.
Global volumes were slightly down in the season to date. Sales to Japan and East Asia were up on the same time last year but sales to Europe were down.
Japan and East Asia were the most promising areas, and Mills said Zespri was planning to increase Japan's volumes past the 11.2 million trays exported in 1996.
Last season, total market returns to growers were up 11 percent at NZ$375 million, or the equivalent of NZ$4.36 a tray. New Zealand represents about 30 percent of the world's kiwifruit production.
